subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should provider-usage runtime temporarily resolve legacy `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles for canonical `openai` usage, or should that legacy state remain doctor/migration-only?
rationale: Repository policy currently says `openai-codex` is legacy migration input, while the PR proof shows a real upgraded status-usage failure that a narrow runtime bridge fixes.

options.title: Approve narrow usage bridge
options.body: Land a rebased version that reads legacy stored profiles only for provider-usage status while preserving canonical `openai` reporting and API-key exclusion.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Close or pause this PR and require affected users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` or follow the broader migration-plan issue/PR instead.

options.title: Fold into migration-plan work
options.body: Use #93180 or a successor to decide route/auth/profile migration holistically before adding any runtime fallback.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow usage bridge
recommendation.body: Land a rebased version that reads legacy stored profiles only for provider-usage status while preserving canonical `openai` reporting and API-key exclusion.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the OpenAI provider unification and legacy-runtime-compatibility boundary that this account previously owned in merged history.
